entries.final_answer: Decision A, union semantics. A proposal.merged fact is valid if EITHER (a) it passes the pre-mission maintainer-merge validation exactly (policy equals the base policy digest, a base-policy maintainer signed it, and its evidence holds enough current maintainer accept decisions), whatever its rule field says, OR (b) it carries a canonical rule claim and passes the new strict rule validation (named rule exists with acceptance rule, signer is one of its executing actors, author and every changed path allowed, no policy or protected-check path changed, and evidence is exactly the qualifying approvals and passing run results, one per counting reviewer and one per trusted runner per pipeline). A fact that passes neither is invalid. A canonical rule claim is exactly one top-level key equal to rule under case folding, spelled exactly rule, holding a JSON string that matches the rule-name grammar; any other shape is no claim and is never a parse error. Facts passing (a) are maintainer merges and are displayed as such; an unverified rule annotation on them may be reported but never makes them invalid. Strict evidence (OQ-5) applies only to path (b). There is no unconditional scan for a rule key: event kinds other than proposal.merged keep the pre-mission decoding and acceptance, so previously valid signed history, including legacy events with unknown or rule-named fields, stays valid, and signed legacy fixtures prove it on every admission surface and against the older client. Older and new clients agree on every fact that passes (a), including a rule-plus-maintainer-decisions fact, which both accept; older clients reject facts valid only through (b), and WP17 tests both. This decision supersedes the parse-time and evidence wording of OQ-5; the rest of OQ-5 (optional rule string on proposal.merged, base policy digest, no new event kind, maintainers-mode facts unchanged) stands.
options: Union: valid if it passes the pre-mission maintainer check whatever its rule field says, or carries a canonical rule claim and passes strict rule validation

Other
entries.question: Amends OQ-5 (decision 01M5VD5Z139R84BBXZM0QXGHJ1) after analysis findings C1, C2 and I1: when is a proposal.merged fact valid, given previously valid signed history and clients built before this mission?
entries.rationale: The analysis showed that a parse-time refusal of rule keys invalidates authenticated legacy bytes (C2), that staged parser and admission work let surfaces disagree about rule-bearing maintainer facts (C1), and that older clients accept a maintainer-signed fact with enough decisions whatever its rule field says (I1). Union semantics keep every fact that passes the pre-mission check valid on every client and confine the new semantics to facts that need the rule path. The maintainer made this decision; the resolved OQ-5 record is immutable in the ledger, so this entry amends it.

entries.final_answer: Event gains Rule string with the tag json:"-", so encoding/json never reads or writes it and every payload decodes and re-encodes exactly as before the mission, including resource kinds, whose strict decoder still refuses an unknown rule key. verifyEvent keeps every existing check and, only for proposal.merged, calls parseMergeRuleClaim, a single top-level token walk that sets Event.Rule when the claim is canonical (exactly one key equal to rule under Unicode case folding, spelled exactly rule, whose value is a JSON string accepted by validPipelineName). Every other shape (absent, null, empty, non-string, case variant, duplicate key, invalid name) leaves Rule empty and is never an error, so such a fact can be valid only through the unchanged maintainer check. Other kinds ignore rule keys as before. encodeAndSign refuses to sign a non-empty Rule on any kind other than proposal.merged or with an invalid name, and emits rule after every other field, so Hubnot only ever writes canonical claims. No new event kind and no protocol version change.

entries.final_answer: Decision B. At every independently landable WP boundary, a surface that does not yet implement path (b) rejects facts valid only through (b) and does not interpret a rule, because it still runs only the unchanged maintainer check. One shared implementation serves every consumer: parseMergeRuleClaim (event.go, WP03), validateRuleMergeFact and the union combinator admitMergeFact (rule_acceptance.go, WP05). Local projection, replication import with the hn serve actor-chain check, and shallow verification each call admitMergeFact and no surface implements its own variant. Shallow verification refuses rule-path facts with an explicit interim refusal from WP07 until WP09 enables its closure rules. On hn serve, WP13 parses hn-rule but evaluateServePush refuses every update that carries it with unsupported-command, as a server built before the mission does, until WP14 replaces that refusal with the rule steps. Boundary fixtures: a valid rule-only fact (accepted exactly by the surfaces that implement (b)), downgrade-shaped maintainer facts with a rule naming an absent rule or an existing standing rule plus enough maintainer decisions (accepted everywhere at every boundary), a defective rule fact (refused everywhere), and a maintainer advancement carrying hn-rule (refused with hosted refs unchanged at every boundary). TestStandingFactBoundary holds the surface table that WP07, WP08 and WP09 update.
options: Fail closed at every boundary through one shared path (b) validator and combinator, with boundary fixtures
Land all admission surfaces atomically in one work package
Other
entries.question: How do independently landable work packages avoid exposing inconsistent validation of rule-bearing facts or of the hn-rule push option (analysis finding C1)?
entries.rationale: Union semantics make the maintainer path the safe default, so a surface that has not been extended already fails closed for rule-only facts. A shared validator and combinator remove the per-surface variants the analysis warned about, and the fixtures make each boundary observable.

entries.final_answer: Decision C. Pre-existing tests are frozen at d881d9bcd0ade4fa1bce91061954a8582e8d9318, the merge commit that brought in the reviewed sync speedup. The audit checks only mission edits: git diff --name-status d881d9b -- *_test.go must list no modified, deleted or renamed test file that exists at d881d9b, only added files. 7a47e6952a427ad7e3a3766c221fd334d9331950 stays the older-client compatibility reference and is not used for the audit. C-001 (go.mod and go.sum unchanged) is audited against d881d9b as well.
options: Freeze at d881d9b and audit only mission edits; keep 7a47e69 as the older-client reference
Freeze at 7a47e69
Other
entries.question: Which commit freezes pre-existing tests for the C-003 and NFR-004 audit, now that the reviewed sync-speedup merge changed replication_borrow_test.go after 7a47e69 (analysis finding I2)?
entries.rationale: The reviewed merge legitimately changed a test file after 7a47e69, so an audit against 7a47e69 fails for a correct implementation. Separating the audit snapshot from the older-binary reference keeps both checks meaningful. The maintainer made this decision.

entries.final_answer: Decision D. Two rerun paths of hn automerge PROPOSAL --rule NAME --execute --remote REMOTE, for standing rules only. (1) Remote repair, unchanged from decision 01M5VF10Q3SQX8WTK2MEN92ZSC: when the hosted tip contains the head, the candidate has no merge fact and the local target still equals the signed base, the command records the missing rule merge fact once with commit equal to the head. (2) Publication-only rerun, new: when the identity is an executing actor of NAME in the base policy and the local store holds a rule merge fact for this proposal that names NAME, is signed by that identity and was admitted through path (b), the command skips the proposal is already recorded as merged blocker of both inspections and the local-equals-hosted check, publishes or republishes the actor chain, and confirms that the hosted branch contains the fact commit. It signs nothing, creates no fact and pushes no branch update; if the hosted branch does not contain the commit it exits 1 and says so. Tests cover interruptions at record and at republish and a repeated rerun. A rerun without --remote keeps the ordinary already-merged refusal. The command-level changes and tests belong to WP19, which also takes the remote repair branch and the interruption table from WP15.
options: Authorized, idempotent publication-only rerun before both merged blockers, in its own WP
Tell the executing actor to run hn sync
Other
entries.question: Amends decision 01M5VF10Q3SQX8WTK2MEN92ZSC after analysis finding I3: how does rerunning hn automerge --execute --remote recover after the rule merge fact was recorded but not, or only partly, published?
entries.rationale: The analysis showed that both inspections stop a rerun at the merged blocker before the promised publication step, so the record row of the interruption table was unreachable. The maintainer specified the publication-only path; a separate WP keeps WP15 within one implementer session.

entries.final_answer: Decision E. NFR-002 has two parts. Fact agreement: the four fact-admission surfaces reach the same verdict on every valid, invalid and legacy merge-fact fixture. Rule-satisfaction agreement: under identical inputs (the same target branch tip, base and target policy, candidate code and fact set), the keyless preview, local execution and the hn serve verdict reach the same rule-satisfaction outcome for every advancement fixture. Executor authorization (identity listed in the rule actors locally; step 13 advance-not-rule-executor on hn serve) and transport and binding checks (hn serve remote identification, selection coverage, local target equals hosted tip, hn-expected-tip and stale tip, fast-forward, code ref hosting, hn-rule support, protected baseline, clean worktree and repository state, the expected-old lease) are excluded from agreement, listed explicitly, and tested on their own. Preview against local execution is tested in WP11, preview against hn serve in WP15, fact agreement in WP16.
options: Rule satisfaction under identical inputs; authorization and transport checks listed and tested separately
Add an actor-aware preview
Other
entries.question: What does NFR-002 agreement compare, given that the keyless preview has no actor input while hn serve checks the requester (analysis finding I4)?
entries.rationale: An unrelated actor obtains an eligible keyless preview of a satisfied rule while its own push must fail advance-not-rule-executor, so agreement over every advancement verdict is unrealizable. Separating the shared rule derivation from requester and transport checks keeps a strong, testable claim. The maintainer made this decision.

entries.final_answer: Commit 7a47e6952a427ad7e3a3766c221fd334d9331950 stays the older-client reference. TestStandingCompatOlderClient builds it once with git archive and go build (GOTOOLCHAIN=local, GOFLAGS empty) into its own t.TempDir() and runs every older-client consumer (opt-out comparison, policy fields, merge facts, legacy history) as a subtest, so the binary outlives all consumers and is removed after the last one; there is no process-wide cache. Each subtest checks that the binary exists before use. It skips with a visible reason under -short and when the commit object or go is absent. The gate runs the whole parent without -short. The tests show that older and new clients agree on every fact that passes the maintainer check, including a rule-plus-maintainer-decisions fact that both accept, accept the same signed legacy events with unknown or rule-named fields, and that the older client rejects facts valid only through the rule path.
options: One owning parent test builds it in its own temporary directory and runs every consumer as a subtest; no process-wide cache
Process-wide sync.Once cache in the first caller temporary directory
Other
entries.question: Amends decision 01M5VF0QVPQ871M0DA8Q0SG5CX after analysis findings U1 and I1: how long does the older-client binary live, and what must the older-client tests show?
entries.rationale: A sync.Once cache that points into the first caller t.TempDir() is deleted by that test cleanup before later consumers run. One owning parent test ties the binary lifetime to its consumers.

entries.final_answer: For every semantic defect row (F01 to F20), the shallow verifier holds the complete closure that path (b) needs: the selected evidence chains and the requests their results answer, the candidate base and head commits with the proposal code ref, the base policy blob and every base-policy pipeline definition at the head. The row passes only when the refusal names the expected check (rule merge <fact> fails <check>, or the maintainer-path refusal for F19 and F20); a shallow dependency gap on a semantic row fails the test. Each semantic row has a valid control with the same selection and object arrangement that the shallow verifier accepts. Missing-dependency rows (F21, F22 and the WP09 gap cases) are a separate table that asserts the dependency kind and recovery guidance.
options: Hydrate a complete closure for semantic rows, assert the derivation check, keep missing-dependency rows separate, add matched valid controls
Count any shallow refusal as success
Other
entries.question: How do shallow-surface rows of the defect matrix prove that semantic defects reach rule derivation instead of passing through an unrelated dependency gap (analysis finding U2)?
entries.rationale: Without matched closure, every shallow negative row could pass through an earlier gap and give a full rejection column without exercising derivation.

entries.final_answer: Each agreement fixture declares its target tip, and the test requires that tip to be equal across the compared surfaces: for WP11 T094 the preview and the execution run in the same clone at that tip; for WP15 T095 E's checked-out main and the hosted main both equal it. The declared tip is the candidate's signed base for every fixture except the target-policy (FR-017) fixture. That fixture follows WP14 T068 step 6: M lands a policy amendment H1 on main, A builds the candidate's head on top of H1 and opens it with --base the older commit, and both compared targets are at H1. The target differs from the signed base by construction and the test does not assert target equals base for it; because the head descends from H1, hn serve passes steps 1 to 7 and refuses at step 7a with protected-destination-policy. Authorization and transport stay in their separate tests as decision 01M5VSEHFH0B1BSJ1NA923FKAA requires.
options: Each fixture declares its target tip; require equality across the compared surfaces; the FR-017 fixture puts both targets at the same amendment commit with the head descending from it
Require target equal to the signed base for every fixture
Other
entries.question: Which target tip does each rule-satisfaction agreement fixture use, given that the FR-017 fixture needs a target policy that differs from the base policy (analysis round 2 finding I4)?
entries.rationale: A universal target-equals-base assertion contradicts a fixture whose target policy must differ from the base policy, because one commit has one policy digest. Equality across surfaces is what NFR-002 requires. Refines the fixture recipe of decision 01M5VSEHFH0B1BSJ1NA923FKAA without changing it. Applied to WP11 T094, WP15 T095 and contracts/serve-rule-advancement.md Agreement.

entries.final_answer: Each legacy fixture asserts its declared verification outcome. L01 to L05 verify successfully. L06, a signed resource event with an added rule key, fails verifyEvent with the existing strict-resource error invalid resource event JSON: unknown field "rule" on the new client and on the 7a47e69 older client, and stays a negative control; the same resource event without the key verifies. Strict resource decoding is not relaxed. WP06 T030 and T091, WP03 T013 and the legacy section of contracts/rule-merge-fact.md state this, and no text says every fixture is accepted.

Require every legacy payload to verify

entries.question: What verification outcome does each legacy history fixture assert, given that L06 is a deliberately invalid resource event (analysis round 2 finding I5)?
entries.rationale: The harness self-test required every raw legacy payload to verify, which L06 cannot do without relaxing strict resource decoding, contradicting C-004 and the legacy contract.

entries.final_answer: Fact-only semantic rows (F01 to F14, F19, F20) use the valid rule merge fact for the same candidate with the defect removed. Candidate-shape rows (F15 to F18) use a corresponding valid candidate built from the same base and files with the defect removed (an allowed author for F15, only allowlisted paths for F16, the src/ change without the manual-path file for F17 and F18), with its reviews, CI requests, run results and merge fact rebound to that candidate. Each control uses the same selection and hydration strategy as its row; both run with a complete closure; the row must still name its intended check, and a refusal through a dependency gap never counts as semantic success. WP06 supplies a Control builder per row; WP09 T041, WP16 T076 and contracts/rule-merge-fact.md use it.
options: Same candidate with the defect removed for fact-only rows; a corresponding valid candidate with rebound reviews, requests, results and merge fact for F15 to F18

Other
entries.question: How is the matched valid control built for semantic defect rows whose defect lies in the candidate itself (F15 to F18), where no change to the fact can remove it (analysis round 2 finding U2)?
entries.rationale: F15 to F18 carry their defect in the signed candidate (author, base and head), so no evidence-only repair yields a valid path (b) fact for the same candidate. Refines the matched-control clause of decision 01M5VSEHFV2K03JJY0NN6DFNAT.

entries.final_answer: F21 builds its own candidate whose only approval is an otherwise qualifying approval by R, the reviewer the default rule counts, signed in R's clone and not published (h.ApproveUnpublished). The CI request and passing result are published, so every other piece of evidence is sufficient. Before publication the verifier reports missing dependency naming the approval with its recovery guidance and the candidate is not merged; after R publishes (h.Publish) and the verifier syncs again, the fact is admitted and hn proposal status reports merged. No R helper runs between F21 preparation and the pre-publication assertion. Applied to WP06 and WP08 T038.
options: Withhold an otherwise qualifying approval from R, keep all other evidence sufficient, assert missing dependency before publication and admission after
Add S to the fixture rule reviewers

entries.question: Which approval does the F21 missing-evidence fixture withhold so that publishing it permits admission under the default rule, which counts only R (analysis round 2 finding U3)?
entries.rationale: S is trusted but not counted by the default rule, so publishing an S approval would leave an evidence-item defect and the promised positive recovery could not occur.

entries.final_answer: Supersedes OQ-1 (decision 01M5VD5PSRW8AVQYE7C8AHEE7Q) and FR-004. proposals.requiredApprovals 0 is allowed with a rule in acceptance mode rule and means the rule needs no approvals: ordinary changes merge on the pipeline gate alone, with no approval from another session. Any value 1 to 64 keeps the confirmed behavior. No policy field is added. Every other blocker still applies: a current trusted change request, a current maintainer rejection, a failed or missing required pipeline result, the author, path and executing-actor limits, the manual path for policy and protected-check changes, and the target-policy check. Because every pipeline requires at least one passing result, policy validation refuses a standing rule with requiredApprovals 0 only when the policy defines no pipeline, so a rule merge always cites gate evidence. A rule merge fact under requiredApprovals 0 may list passing run results only; the strict path (b) evidence rules are otherwise unchanged, and approvals from counted reviewers, when present, are still listed. Clients that predate the rule fields still reject such facts.
options: Allow requiredApprovals 0 under acceptance rule; the rule then needs no approvals and the pipeline gate and every veto still apply
Keep the OQ-1 refusal
Add a rule-level approval threshold
Other
entries.question: Amends OQ-1 (decision 01M5VD5PSRW8AVQYE7C8AHEE7Q): may a rule with acceptance rule be used when proposals.requiredApprovals is 0, so ordinary changes merge on the pipeline gate alone?
entries.rationale: Maintainer decision (Andrew, 2026-10-30): ordinary changes must be able to merge on the gate alone, configurable through the existing proposals.requiredApprovals field. The resolved OQ-1 record is immutable in the ledger, so this entry amends it. The pipeline requirement for requiredApprovals 0 was chosen by the implementer under delegated instruction so that a standing rule never merges with no evidence at all; it adds a validation, not a field.
